title: VMPX
meta.lead: A bridge for VMPX between Ethereum and the X1 blockchain, built by the XEN community. Every VMPXe on X1 is backed 1:1 by original VMPX locked on Ethereum, and anyone can verify the backing live.

sections.title: What VMPX Bridge is
sections.lead: The bridge moves VMPX from Ethereum to X1 and back, 1:1, with no account and no middleman.

blocks.text: All you need is two wallets: MetaMask on the Ethereum side and Backpack or X1 Wallet on the X1 side. There is no registration: your wallet is your identity, and you sign every step yourself.

text: , an open bridge standard with external audits, not on custom cryptography. It runs publicly on testnet (Sepolia ⇄ X1 testnet). Mainnet will launch with a cap of about 1,000 USD in the bridge, raised step by step.

sections.title: Why we are building it
sections.lead: The XEN community has waited years for a path into X1. The announced VMPX bridge was never delivered, so we are building it ourselves.

sections.title: How it works
sections.lead: Original VMPX stays locked on Ethereum; on X1 its counterpart VMPXe circulates and is burned on the way back.

blocks.text: You approve exactly the transfer amount, the bridge contract (lockbox) locks the VMPX and sends a message. Validators attest it, and the program on X1 mints VMPXe to your address.
You burn VMPXe on X1, the message is attested, and the lockbox on Ethereum unlocks VMPX to your address.

items: — a collateral contract on Ethereum, a Token-2022 token on X1. Our own code is limited to the fee router, the fee hook and configuration.
— VMPX on Ethereum has 18 decimals, VMPXe on X1 has 9. A transfer amount can have at most 9 decimals; only the 3% fee is rounded down.
— on testnet Ethereum → X1 takes about 1 min, X1 → Ethereum 20–30 s. On mainnet Ethereum → X1 will take a few minutes (safe number of blocks).

blocks.label: Backing rule
blocks.text: Lockbox balance on Ethereum ≥ VMPXe supply on X1 + transfers in flight. The monitor checks this continuously and the site shows it live.

sections.title: Security
sections.lead: Security is layered: each layer assumes the previous one may fail.

text: — every message passes three checks at once: attestation by the required number of validators, no pause, and the daily limit. On mainnet we plan 5 of 7 independent attestations, with keys in KMS modules.
— the daily limit caps traffic per day, and a cap limits the total amount in the bridge (about 1,000 USD at launch).

blocks.label: Automatic pause
blocks.text: Every 30 s the monitor matches each mint on X1 to a deposit on Ethereum, and each withdrawal to a burn on X1 — by message ID, across two independent data sources. Hard evidence of a violation pauses the bridge in both directions and the team is alerted immediately. From violation to pause takes up to about 2 minutes in practice: detection every 30 s, decision every 60 s; sending the pause took 15 s in our drill.

sections.title: Fees and flow of funds
sections.lead: You sign every step yourself, and before signing you see what you send, the fee, and what arrives.

text: Example: you send 10,000 VMPX from Ethereum and receive
on X1, plus Ethereum gas and 0.0002 ETH. In the other direction the full VMPX amount arrives.

blocks.text: The 3% VMPX fee goes to the LP Treasury in the same transaction, intended for VMPX/XNT liquidity on X1. The 0.0002 ETH fee covers the gas of the relayer delivering the transfer to X1. The XNT fee goes on mainnet to the project multisig on X1. The treasury balance is public and shown on the site.

sections.lead: We do not ask for trust — everything important can be checked yourself.

blocks.title: How we reviewed the code
body: The project has had no paid external audit. The code went through

of independent AI-assisted reviews (every finding fixed or documented), a review by an independent reviewer, contract analysis with Slither, Foundry tests, end-to-end tests with real wallets on every site version since November 2026, manual community testing, and a drill of the automatic pause on the live test bridge.

sections.title: Risks
sections.lead: Every cross-chain bridge carries risk. We state it plainly.

items: — no review guarantees the absence of bugs. That is why mainnet launches with a small cap.
— compromising the required number of validator keys would allow a forged message to be attested. Auto-pause is meant to stop the bridge, but may not act before the first damage.
— losing them can block administration; compromising them could allow a harmful change. The timelock gives 48 h to react.
— a bug or outage in Hyperlane, Ethereum or X1 can halt transfers.
— while paused, Ethereum → X1 is rejected and X1 → Ethereum waits until unpause. When the daily limit is used up, a large transfer waits for it to refill.
— the bridge guarantees 1:1 backing, not the price or liquidity of VMPXe on X1.

blocks.text: Use the bridge only with amounts you can afford to lose, especially early on.

sections.title: What's next
sections.lead: We move in stages — the next step only once the previous one runs stably.

items: — we open the code; the community tests the bridge and reports bugs.
— permissions in a Ledger-backed multisig, validators on our own infrastructure with keys in KMS, a permission-change monitor, a bridge cap, a final review of the whole codebase.
— launch with a cap of about 1,000 USD and a low daily limit; limits raised gradually via the timelock, visible in advance. Then VMPX/XNT liquidity on X1.

blocks.text: We do not give fixed dates: mainnet timing depends on test results, not the calendar.
